headline: PHP2Shell CISA deadline is tomorrow; PolyShell breaches hundreds of Magento stores as Brotli exploit traffic emerges

bullets.text: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) is exploited in the wild and remains the top story at 8 outlets. CISA's federal due date is tomorrow, 2026-10-29. Fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35.

PolyShell attacks on Adobe Commerce have breached hundreds of stores, and exploit traffic for the Brotli 'HTTP2Shell' flaw has emerged. CVE-2026-48356 (Magento) and CVE-2026-111497 (Brotli) are in CISA KEV, due 2026-11-10; Microsoft shipped emergency .NET patches.
New: a University of Copenhagen data breach exposes data of 525,000 people. Canada's Privacy Commissioner is also investigating a breach involving Crime Stoppers.

Japan's GMO is offering a $1 million bounty over a breach of its FX trading cloud after urging customers to shut down PCs. Ransomware is still disrupting care at UNM Health and hit Bajaj Hospital in India. The ShinyHunters-exploited PeopleSoft zero-day (CVE-2026-35273) is three chained flaws.

Supply chain: the LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromise on PyPI and Docker began with an exposed master key. A worm armed 42 GitHub repos, 'Gheist' uses stolen GitHub tokens to steal cloud secrets, and the Convertr analytics script was hijacked to steal card data.
Still active: Tailscale's SSH root-escalation fixes, HPE's critical networking patches and Apple's CoreGraphics zero-day backports for older iPhones. Last 7 days at 1.02x the 90-day average.

actions: Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 before CISA's 2026-10-29 due date, rebuild images that bundle PHP, and check exposed PHP hosts for compromise.
Patch Adobe Commerce and Magento for CVE-2026-48356 now and check stores for webshells and unexpected uploaded files.
Apply Microsoft's emergency .NET patches for Brotli CVE-2026-111497 and track fixes from other software that bundles Brotli.
Apply Oracle's fixes for the PeopleSoft chain (CVE-2026-35273) and review PeopleSoft access logs for signs of data theft.
Search lockfiles, images and CI caches for litellm 1.107.0; if it ran, treat the host as compromised and rotate every credential it could read.
Update Tailscale, apply HPE and Apple updates, and audit payment-page scripts and GitHub tokens.
